Senses.Explanation: To seek fire is the action in the repeatedly raised answer, “the fire-boy comes seeking fire.” Fayan Wenyi refuses Xuanze’s explanation that this simply means using fire to seek fire or using oneself to seek oneself; elsewhere masters pair seeking fire with striking or carving ice, making it an image of a search whose chosen means cannot yield what is sought. Qinglin Shiqian first answers Xuanze’s question about his own self with “the fire-boy comes seeking fire.” When Xuanze later explains the line to Fayan as fire seeking fire and self seeking self, Fayan says that understanding will not do. Fayan then has Xuanze ask the question again and gives the same answer himself. The repeated words therefore survive while Xuanze’s explanatory menu is expressly rejected. Feiyin Tongrong pairs “carving ice to seek fire” with “steaming sand to make rice.” The Questions Posed to the Chan School later classifies the fire-boy answer as a living phrase while recording the rejected fire-with-fire explanation. These are one lexical action, not separate senses: the fire-boy case, seeking fire with fire, and seeking it from ice vary the seeker and means while retaining the act of seeking fire.
